title: SPECIFICATION, TRACEABILITY, AND MANAGEMENT
meta: Client Site: Deniz Construction Limited, Ishanyu Bushenyi Road, Mbarara

blocks.text: PART 1: SOFTWARE REQUIREMENTS SPECIFICATION
1. INTRODUCTION
1.1 Purpose

This document specifies the functional and non functional requirements for the Deniz Construction Management System (DCMS). It serves as the blueprint for the SWE1205 Database Programming implementation and the final Grand Presentation.
1.2 Scope

The DCMS is a Dual Phase Operations Management System. During the day, it functions as a Real Time Point of Sale to process individual sales, calculate VAT, update inventory and print physical receipts for customers. In the evening, it functions as an End of Day Reconciliation Engine, allowing the Sales Manager to review recorded payment activity by channel, log operational expenses, compute cash variances and generate a final daily summary report for the Business Owner.
1.3 Explicitly Excluded Features
Based on verified ground observations, the following features are strictly excluded to prevent scope creep.

items: Credit and Debtors Module. The business operates on a strict no credit policy. All payments are made upfront.
Real Time Remote Monitoring Dashboard. The Business Owner visits the site daily. Remote access is limited to asynchronous historical review.
Complex Logistics and Delivery Tracking. Customers transport their own purchased goods by truck.

blocks.text: 2. OVERALL DESCRIPTION
2.1 User Classes and Characteristics

runs.text: Sales Manager (Primary User).
Acts as supervisor, cashier, payroll distributor and record keeper. Requires a system that reduces end of day reconciliation workload and automates receipt generation during the day.
Business Owner.
Visits the site daily. Requires clear operational summaries followed by financial reconciliation and long term trend analysis.
Site Workers.
Status is a documented limitation. Never spoken to. System requires only a simplified interface for the Sales Manager to log their daily attendance for payroll.
URA (External Regulator).
Dictates tax compliance, VAT and receipting standards. System must ensure financial outputs meet audit expectations.
Customers and Builders.
Purchase blocks and pavers. Pay upfront. Transport their own goods by truck. Require quick receipt generation to minimize loading delays.

blocks.text: 2.2 General Constraints

items: The system must run on the existing single office laptop (assumed baseline standard office specification).
The system must operate in an offline first mode for real time receipting during the day and batch reconciliation in the evening.
The system must support multi channel payment tracking (Cash, Mobile Money, Bank Deposit) with separate totals by business date and channel.
All financial data must be backed up automatically to a secure cloud destination each evening after reconciliation.

blocks.text: 2.3 Assumptions and Dependencies

items: The current VAT rate of 18 percent is assumed to remain stable. The rate will be stored in a configurable System Settings table rather than hardcoded.
The Sales Manager possesses basic digital literacy to operate a mouse, keyboard and web browser.
The site has intermittent internet connectivity sufficient for an evening cloud backup.
The single office laptop meets the minimum hardware requirements to run a local database server and application.

blocks.text: 3. FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS

All requirements use a unified hierarchical ID scheme to ensure traceability. The format is REQ-FUN-<MODULE>-<NN> for functional requirements and REQ-NFR-<MODULE>-<NN> for non functional requirements.
3.1 Module A: Real Time Transactional Sales and Receipting

runs.text: REQ-FUN-SAL-01 (Transactional Sale Entry).

The system shall allow the Sales Manager to post a sale to an open business date with one or more product lines, each with a positive quantity and a unit price, and one payment method (Cash, Mobile Money or Bank Deposit). The sale and all stock changes shall commit together.
REQ-FUN-SAL-02 (Automated VAT Calculation).
Upon saving a sale, the system shall automatically calculate the 18 percent Value Added Tax on the subtotal using a database stored procedure and display the total amount.
REQ-FUN-SAL-03 (Sequential Receipt Generation).

The system shall generate a unique, sequential Receipt ID for every transaction. The system shall retain the original receipt and require a reason for every void, refund or correction. An erroneous entry on an open day may be voided if no payment was received and no goods were released. Record a full refund only when the full payment was returned through the original channel. Record corrections to a closed sale on an open business date and preserve the original close.
REQ-FUN-SAL-04 (Physical Receipt Printing).

After the sale commits, the system shall immediately format and send a physical receipt to the attached printer containing the sequential ID, date, customer name, product description, quantity, unit price, subtotal, VAT, total amount and payment method.
REQ-FUN-SAL-05 (Inventory Deduction Trigger).

The system shall deduct stock for each sale line. If any quantity exceeds the stock available for that product, the system shall reject the entire sale. It shall flag stock at or below the reorder level.

blocks.text: 3.2 Module B: End of Day Reconciliation and Deficit Resolution

runs.text: REQ-FUN-REC-01 (Daily Payment Activity by Channel).

The system shall show separate recorded payment activity for Cash, Mobile Money and Bank Deposit for the selected business date. Each channel total shall include sales recorded for that date, less entry voids for sales of that date and refunds paid that date. Mobile Money and Bank Deposit totals represent recorded activity. External statement matching is outside this design.
REQ-FUN-REC-02 (Operational Expense Logging).
The system shall allow the Sales Manager to log zero or more individual cash expenses against an open business date during the day or at evening reconciliation.
REQ-FUN-REC-03 (Expected Cash Computation).

The system shall calculate expected cash for the selected business date as recorded opening cash plus net cash sales activity minus logged cash expenses. Net cash sales activity excludes entry errors voided on the same date and subtracts cash refunds paid that date. A bookkeeping correction to an earlier date does not reduce today's expected cash. Opening cash defaults to zero and can be recorded before closing if a float is carried. The site practice for carrying a float is unconfirmed.
REQ-FUN-REC-04 (Variance Reporting).

The system shall require a physical cash count of zero or more. Variance equals actual cash minus expected cash. A negative variance is a deficit and a positive variance is a surplus. The Sales Manager shall provide a nonblank explanation when the variance is nonzero.
REQ-FUN-REC-05 (Daily Summary Report Generation).

The system shall finalize one Daily Summary Report per business date. Closing shall save the payment totals for all three channels, opening cash, expenses, expected cash, actual cash, variance and explanation together. The report shall include trucks dispatched, blocks sold and workers present. Repeating a successful close shall return the saved result. A closed business date shall reject new financial postings.

blocks.text: 3.3 Module C: Attendance and Daily Payroll

runs.text: REQ-FUN-ATT-01 (Worker Attendance Logging).

The system shall allow the Sales Manager to log a worker as Present for a given date using a simplified interface with large visual icons. A unique Worker ID and Date combination shall be enforced to prevent duplicate daily entries.
REQ-FUN-ATT-02 (Daily Payroll Eligibility).

The system shall utilize a database query joining the Workers and Attendance tables to generate the daily payroll eligibility list, including only workers with a verified Present status for that date.

blocks.text: 3.4 Module D: URA Compliance and Reporting

runs.text: REQ-FUN-TAX-01 (URA Summary Report).

The system shall generate a URA Compliance Summary Report showing posted sales, their recorded VAT and separately identified adjustments for the selected period. The filing treatment of refunds and corrections remains subject to verification against URA guidance.

blocks.text: 3.5 Module E: Data Backup and Recovery

runs.text: REQ-FUN-BAK-01 (Automated Nightly Backup).
The system shall execute an encrypted database backup to a secure cloud destination each evening after the reconciliation session is closed, ensuring disaster recovery for the single laptop.

blocks.text: 4. NON FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS
4.1 Performance and Reliability

runs.text: REQ-NFR-PER-01 (Offline Resilience).

The system shall support full real time transactional processing and receipt printing without an active internet connection. Data shall be persisted locally and the evening cloud backup shall queue and retry upon connectivity restoration.
REQ-NFR-PER-02 (Hardware Compatibility).
The application shall be optimized to run efficiently on the existing office laptop. Report generation shall target completion within a reasonable time for the business context.

blocks.text: 4.2 Security and Access Control

runs.text: REQ-NFR-SEC-01 (Role Based Access Control).

The system shall enforce strict RBAC at both the database and application layers. The Sales Manager shall post sales, expenses, adjustments and reconciliation through authorized operations that enforce the business date lock. The role shall have no direct write access to those financial tables. The role may maintain attendance. The Owner role shall have SELECT on all tables and views including restricted views for Total Profit and Tax Liability.
REQ-NFR-SEC-02 (Immutable Audit Trail).

The system shall maintain an immutable Audit Log table recording the User ID, Timestamp, Action Type (for example, VOID SALE, LOG EXPENSE) and Previous Value for any modification to financial records.

blocks.text: 4.3 Usability

runs.text: REQ-NFR-USR-01 (Low Literacy Interface).
The attendance and expense logging interfaces shall utilize high contrast visual icons and require minimal text input, ensuring usability for workers with varying literacy levels.

blocks.text: PART 3: VALIDATION AND VERIFICATION PLAN
1. Validation (Are We Building the Right Product?)
Validation confirms the requirements meet the actual business needs of Deniz Construction.

items: Walkthrough with Sales Manager: Review the Real Time Sale flow and End of Day Reconciliation flow against the observed As Is workflow. Confirm the Dual Phase model matches her mental model of daily operations.

Owner Review of Daily Summary Report: Present the generated Daily Summary Report mockup to the Business Owner. Confirm the Operational Metrics First structure (Trucks, Blocks, Workers) followed by Financial Summary matches what he reviews during his daily evening visits.

URA Compliance Check: Verify the URA Summary Report output format against a blank URA VAT form (obtained from the site or standard template). Confirm all required fields are present and VAT calculation matches the 18 percent standard.

Gap Closure Verification: For each documented gap (Workers, Receipt Fields), verify that the stated assumption (for example, standard URA fiscal fields for receipts) is acceptable to the primary stakeholder (Sales Manager) during the walkthrough.

blocks.text: 2. Verification (Are We Building the Product Right?)
Verification confirms the implementation correctly implements the specified requirements.

items: Unit Test: CalculateVAT Stored Procedure. Input: Subtotal = 100,000. Expected Output: VAT = 18,000, Total = 118,000. Edge case: Subtotal = 0 returns VAT = 0.

Inventory and atomic sale posting. Sell two products and check each deduction. Retry with an oversold line and verify the sale, all stock changes and any alert roll back. Test zero, negative and exact stock quantities.

Sale adjustments. Void an unpaid entry error and verify the original receipt remains visible, stock is restored and the entry is removed from net payment activity. Record a refund on an open date and verify the linked adjustment, stock for goods returned and unchanged prior close. Reject a duplicate full adjustment. Correct a prior day entry error and verify current expected cash and the closed snapshot stay unchanged.

Payment totals and closing. Post sales in three channels across two business dates. Verify each channel and date is isolated. Close one date while another session attempts to post to it. Verify the post is included or rejected, a second close returns the saved result and the other date is unaffected.
Expected cash. With zero opening cash, cash sales of 500,000 and expenses of 50,000, expected cash is 450,000. With an opening float of 20,000 and a cash refund of 10,000, expected cash is 460,000.

Variance. Actual cash of 445,000 against expected cash of 450,000 gives a deficit of 5,000 with a negative stored variance. Reject a blank explanation for a nonzero variance and accept a blank explanation at zero variance. Reject missing or negative cash counts.
Unit Test: Attendance Unique Daily Constraint. Attempt to insert duplicate (Worker_ID, Date). Verify database constraint rejection.
Unit Test: RBAC Enforcement. Attempt SELECT on Total_Profit view as Sales Manager role. Verify permission denied. Attempt same as Owner role. Verify permission granted.

Integration Test: End to End Daily Workflow. Simulate 10 sales across all payment channels, 3 expenses, 5 attendance logs. Run evening reconciliation. Verify Daily Summary Report matches manual calculation.

blocks.text: PART 4: REQUIREMENTS MANAGEMENT PLAN
1. Change Control Process
Since the business is a small SME, the Change Control Board (CCB) consists of the Business Owner and Group K. No external approvals are required.

items: Change Request Submission: Any stakeholder may submit a change request describing the proposed change, the reason and the expected impact.
Impact Analysis: Group K assesses the impact on the SRS, database schema, stored procedures, triggers, views and UI. The analysis includes effort estimation and risk assessment.
Decision: The Business Owner approves, rejects, or defers the change. Approved changes are assigned a Change Request ID and scheduled.
Implementation: The change is implemented in the SRS, the database schema and the application code. The Requirements Traceability Matrix is updated to reflect the new or modified requirement.

blocks.text: 2. Version Control

All requirements documents, database schemas and source code are version controlled in the project Git repository (https://github.com/mugmarp/requirements-engineering-project-exercise). Each change to the SRS is committed with a message referencing the Change Request ID.
3. Requirements Attributes

Each requirement carries the following attributes: ID, Title, Type (Functional or Non Functional), Module, Priority (High, Medium, Low), Status (Proposed, Approved, Implemented, Verified), Source (Elicitation Fact, Business Assumption, Gap Synthesis) and Traceability Links.
PART 5: DATABASE DESIGN SPECIFICATION (SWE1205)
1. Conceptual Data Model (ER Diagram Entities)
The following entities form the normalized relational schema (Third Normal Form). The Products entity now reflects the actual Deniz Construction Limited product catalogue.

rows: Name, Category (Solid Block, Hollow Block, Paver, Kerb), Dimensions, Unit_Price, VAT_Rate, Unit_of_Measure (Pieces, Square Meters, Bundles), Current_Stock, Reorder_Level
Business_Date, Date_Time, Customer_Name, Subtotal, VAT, Total, Payment_Method

One final record per closed Business_Day

blocks.text: 2. Stored Procedures
CalculateVAT(Subtotal DECIMAL) RETURNS DECIMAL: Returns Subtotal * (SELECT Setting_Value FROM System_Settings WHERE Setting_Key = VAT_RATE). The VAT rate is stored in System_Settings, not hardcoded.

CloseDay accepts Business_Date, Actual_Cash, Explanation and Closed_By. In one InnoDB transaction it locks the selected Business_Day row. If closed, it returns the saved reconciliation. Otherwise it validates the count and explanation, calculates the daily totals and saves the report snapshot and Closed status together. An error rolls back the close. Opening cash changes use the same business date lock and require Open status. Each new date has its own activity and opening cash.
3. Stock Trigger and Transaction Rules

An AFTER INSERT trigger on Sales_Items rejects nonpositive quantities. It deducts NEW.Quantity from Products.Current_Stock for NEW.Product_ID only if enough stock remains. If no row is updated, it raises an error. Stock at or below Reorder_Level is flagged using the resulting product balance.

PostSale and cash expense posting must lock the same Business_Day row as CloseDay and require Open status. PostSale saves the header and all lines in one InnoDB transaction and rolls back on any failure. Receipt printing follows commit. Compute payment totals from posted records for each date and channel.

RecordSaleAdjustment locks the effective Business_Day and the original sale in one transaction. The project design supports one full adjustment per sale and refunds through the original channel. Net_Amount and VAT_Amount are signed reversals of the original subtotal and VAT. Refund payment activity uses the combined amount. For an entry error, reverse the recorded sale amount and VAT and restore stock only for goods that were never released. For a refund, require confirmation that the original total was returned through the original channel and restore only goods returned to stock. Preserve closed snapshots. Record the reason and audit entry in the same transaction.
4. Views

Daily_Payment_Activity groups original sales and signed adjustments by business date and payment method. Count a same day entry void or an actual refund once in payment activity. Show corrections of prior day entry errors separately because they do not move money on the current date. The original entry remains visible in the transaction history.
URA_Summary reports recorded sales and VAT with linked adjustments shown separately by effective date. Filing treatment of refunds and corrections requires validation.
Payroll_Eligibility: Joins Workers and Attendance to list workers Present on a given date with their Daily_Rate.
Total_Profit (Owner Only): Restricted view computing net revenue after recorded adjustments minus expenses per period. SELECT permission granted to Owner role only.
Tax_Liability (Owner Only): Restricted view showing recorded VAT and related adjustments for the period. SELECT permission granted to Owner role only.
Daily_Reconciliation_Report reads the saved Daily_Reconciliation snapshot for the selected business date.
